newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Schmidheiny withdraws from small caps.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Schmidheiny withdraws from small caps.

text.p: Stephan Schmidheiny, the Swiss green industrialist, is gradually withdrawing from small, domestically-oriented Swiss companies in favour of globally-active Swiss companies, a representative said.
Swiss banks, however, are not seen as having much investment potential, Jacques Kaegi, spokesman for Schmidheiny, told Reuters upon inquiries.
Schmidheiny had decided on this new strategy for his investment companies Unotec Holding AG and Anova Holding AG in January, he added.

Although Schmidheiny will withdraw from the board of electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG in April, Kaegi said the industrialist planned to maintain his stake of 4.3 percent in Swiss ABB.
Earlier today Valora Holding AG, a diversified Swiss company, said Schmidheiny's Anova had reduced its stake to less than five percent from almost 10 percent by selling the shares on the bourse.
"We mainly want to hold portfolio participations in smaller companies, which means below five percent," Kaegi said.
Kaegi also said the Schmidheiny group recently had sold its stake of around 12 percent in BB Industrie.
But Kaegi said Anova, which owns around four percent of Swiss retailer Globus, would probably retain the stake.
Schmidheiny's recent sale of 1.12 million registered shares in UBS illustrates that he no longer believes the large banks have major potential.
Kaegi acknowledged that the sale in January had led to a loss of almost 20 million Swiss francs.
Schmidheiny bought his stake in UBS in February 1996 from BK Vision, part of Martin Ebner's BK investment group.
Jaegi said examples of large, international Swiss firms are Novartis AG, Roche Holding AG and Nestle SA.
"But we will also remain with ABB in the long term," Kaegi said.
In addition to Anova und Unotec, Schmidheiny also owns Nueva, a holding company with majority stakes in 40 building and forestry companies in Latin America.

Schmidheiny is one of Switzerland's wealthiest individuals and is part of the United Nation's-appointed High Level Advisory Board on Sustainable Development, which advises the UN on development policies and their environmental impact.
